title: Autotune Sentinel: guided recovery, validation fences, and cost-safety runbook for batching/cache tuning
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: After an autotune rollout on 2026-02-20 that recommended aggressive batching and prefix-KV cache demotion rules for a subset of traffic, we observed a 12% regression in 95th percentile tail latency for low-QPS customers and several throttled requests in Dedicated pools. This ticket captures the incident follow-up, a structured Sentinel approach for safe applies and rollbacks, validation fences for cost savings recommendations, and a prescriptive runbook for on-call and SRE teams. The goal is to enable automated cost-optimizations while guaranteeing bounded latency and a deterministic rollback path.
timeline:
2026-02-20: Autotune deployment v2.3 rolled to 20% of production traffic (canary).
2026-02-20 10:42 UTC: Alerts triggered - p95 latency up 9% on canary cohort (region us-west-2).
2026-02-20 11:05 UTC: Autotune completed additional batch/cache changes and expanded to 60% traffic for the same cohort.
2026-02-20 11:18 UTC: Increased request timeouts and several capacity throttles observed in Dedicated pools.
2026-02-20 11:40 UTC: Immediate manual rollback to baseline configs for affected cohort.
2026-02-21: Initial RCA scoping and data collection.
2026-02-25: Formal postmortem kickoff and assignment of follow-ups.
root_cause: Two simultaneous issues combined to create the regression: (1) Autotune suggested a micro-batching policy that increased per-request queuing for short-lived low-token requests, worsening tail behavior under bursty arrivals. (2) A newly-introduced cache demotion heuristic evicted hot prefixes prematurely on Dedicated pools with skewed key distributions, increasing cold-start KV lookups and kernel recomputations. The canary expansion logic lacked a hard validation fence on p95 and throttling rates before increasing traffic percentage, allowing amplification of the regression.
mitigations_deployed: Immediate rollback of autotune recommendations for the affected cohort (manual revert). Tuned canary ramp policy to 10% max until additional validations pass. Added temporary circuit-breaker to prevent autotune from making 'demote' decisions on Dedicated pools with fewer than 10k active prefixes. Notified customers that experienced throttling and opened support tickets for three affected accounts.
permanent_fixes:
1) Implement Sentinel validation fences: require multiple pass criteria (p95 change < +3%, throttle_count delta < 5/min, error_rate change < +0.5%) over a 30-minute window before any canary ramp step.
2) Improve cache-demote heuristic to use weighted prefix hotness and a minimum residency time (configurable), preventing premature eviction under skew.
3) Add autotune dry-run mode that performs offline cost/latency simulations using sampled production traces pre-apply.
4) Autoscaler/backpressure integration: autotune must query Dedicated pool throttle metrics before suggesting batch increases.
5) Canary rollback fences: automated rollback if any validation criteria fail, with a human-in-loop alert for P1 anomalies.
6) Add explicit 'safety token' that prevents concurrent autotune recommendations on overlapping cohorts.
runbook_steps: Detect: Watch autotune-canary dashboards (dashboards/autotune/canary-overview) and subscribe to p95, throttle_count, error_rate alerts for canary cohorts.
Isolate: If p95 > baseline + 5% OR throttle_count spike > 10/min, immediately cut traffic for the canary cohort to 0% using routing flag: 'autotune.canary.<cohort>.traffic=0'.

Rollback: Trigger autotune revert job: PATCH /internal/autotune/v1/cohorts/<id>/revert with reason and correlation id. Confirm revert PR merged in GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autotune/pulls. Document the revert in incident notes with timestamps.
Validate: After revert, validate p95 and throttle_count return to baseline for 30 minutes. If not, escalate to SRE lead and open a dedicated incident channel (#inc-ot-autotune).

Post-incident: Run offline replay for the failed cohort with changed knobs and record simulated p95 distribution. Attach simulation artifacts to the ticket and to Confluence page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Autotune+Sentinel+Postmortem.
Deploy safeguards: Enable guardrails in autotune config: 'max_batch_increase_pct', 'min_prefix_residency_seconds', 'dedicated_pool_demote_forbidden' for 2 weeks while monitoring.
Communication: Send incident summary to affected customers and internal stakeholders within 48 hours; include mitigation steps and timeline.
Close: Only close the ticket after verification of permanent fixes and a 14-day regression-free observation window on representative workloads.
